hero.h1: Kitchen Remodeling in Martinsburg, WV, Planned in Our Showroom
hero.subheadline: Pick cabinets, counters and vanities in person at our 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive. Our own in-house team then installs everything, from toe-kicks to hardware.

image.alt: Kitchen remodeling Martinsburg WV: Petrasek family kitchen with Muted Moss green base cabinets, Wicker-finish wood uppers and island, Tyrol quartz counters and a chimney range hood

intro.h2: A Martinsburg showroom with 31 years behind it
paragraphs: Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths has handled kitchen remodeling in Martinsburg, WV and across the Eastern Panhandle since 1995. You start in a 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive, where you can open cabinet doors, compare countertops and stand at real vanities. Then the in-house team builds it.

The firm leans on American-made cabinetry from makers such as KraftMaid. Its project write-ups list each door style and finish, like a Muted Moss and Wicker two-tone kitchen in Martinsburg or a load-bearing wall moved four feet in Harpers Ferry. Reviewers praise the guidance through layouts and selections, and the clear communication.

services.h2: Kitchens and baths, from design to the last cabinet pull

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Full tear-outs, wall removals and layout changes, carried out by Mountaineer's own team. In Harpers Ferry, the Jackson kitchen gained an open plan when a load-bearing wall moved four feet on two LVL beams. It was finished with Woodhaven Shaker cabinets and Calacatta Arno quartz.

image.alt: Harpers Ferry, WV kitchen remodel with walnut-tone Shaker cabinets, white quartz counters, brass faucet and gas cooktop

items.name: Cabinets and Countertops
items.blurb: Choose semi-custom or traditional cabinetry in the showroom, with brands like KraftMaid and Brighton Cabinetry. Counters come in quartz, stone, wood, solid surface, laminate or concrete. In Falling Waters, the Wiggins kitchen paired Shortbread maple base cabinets with wood accents.

image.alt: Falling Waters, WV kitchen with white KraftMaid cabinets, wood-tone island with seating, glass pendant lights and a French door

items.name: Bathroom Remodels
items.blurb: Primary baths, guest baths and powder rooms, planned around your budget, timeline and style. The team handles layout changes, new windows, closets and knee walls. A Charles Town family came back after their kitchen to have the bath gutted and rebuilt.

image.alt: Primary bathroom remodel with freestanding white soaking tub, wood-look tile wainscot and frameless glass walk-in shower

items.name: Custom Tile Showers
items.blurb: Showers are built on Schluter pans and wrapped in Kerdi waterproofing membrane before any tile goes up. In Harpers Ferry, the Reap master bath got a 72-inch curbless shower in 12x24 tile, two niches and Ditra-Heat floor heating with a 10-year manufacturer warranty.

image.alt: Harpers Ferry, WV curbless walk-in shower with large white 12x24 tile in a brick pattern, tiled niche and glass door

items.name: New Construction Kitchens and Baths
items.blurb: Building a new home? Mountaineer draws the floor plan for the new kitchen or bath and installs the cabinets, fixtures and lighting. Kitchen styles range from traditional and Craftsman to cottage, Mediterranean, transitional and modern, all on view in the showroom.

image.alt: Cottage-style kitchen with white cabinets, open wood shelves, wood range hood, butcher block island and retro green refrigerator

why_choose_us.h2: Why Eastern Panhandle families choose Mountaineer

items.title: See it before you buy it
items.text: The 5,000 sq. ft. showroom on Rock Cliff Drive is the only one of its kind in the area. You can open the cabinets and feel the countertops before you decide.

items.title: Our own crew installs
items.text: Every project is handled in-house from start to finish. That includes demo, plumbing changes, drywall, trim and hardware, with no hand-off to strangers halfway through.

items.title: American-made materials
items.text: Cabinetry and materials on every job are American-made. Recent kitchens used all-plywood boxes and soft-close hardware from lines such as KraftMaid and Woodhaven.

items.title: A team that has stayed
items.text: Owner Ben DeOms has worked alongside most of the crew for five, ten or more years. Google reviewers name Brandon and Eric for patient, careful design guidance.

about.h2: From summer job at 16 to owner
about.text: Ben DeOms first walked into Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths at 16. He worked summers, evenings and weekends through high school and learned the trade beside skilled craftsmen. He eventually took over the business, which has served Martinsburg for more than 31 years. Ben says he wants to keep the quality and integrity the previous owners built, with American-made materials on every job. Under his ownership the company opened its new showroom and is taking on more higher-end projects. Project manager Buck Day, sales and design lead Brandon Cooley, salesman Patrick Carter and office manager Heidi Shank round out the team.

image.alt: Ben DeOms, owner of Mountaineer Kitchens & Baths in Martinsburg, WV

process.h2: How a Mountaineer project comes together

steps.title: Start at the showroom
steps.text: Stop in or book a time to talk through your goals, needs and inspiration while you look at cabinets, counters and vanities in person.

steps.title: Layout and selections
steps.text: The designer reviews layout options, whether galley, L-shaped or U-shaped, and guides your choices of materials, finishes, fixtures and paint colors.

steps.title: Ordering and scheduling
steps.text: Planning, design, ordering and scheduling make up most of the 3 to 6 months a kitchen project takes from start to finish.

steps.title: In-house installation
steps.text: Once work starts, a typical kitchen takes about 2 to 3 weeks. Mountaineer's own team handles demo, trades, cabinets, trim and hardware.

steps.title: The reveal
steps.text: You walk into the finished room. For the team, seeing a client's reaction to the start-to-finish change is the best part of the job.

service_area.text: Mountaineer is based in Martinsburg and works for homeowners across Berkeley, Jefferson and Morgan counties in West Virginia's Eastern Panhandle. Recent projects include kitchens in Martinsburg, Falling Waters, Charles Town and Harpers Ferry. There are also custom tile baths in Harpers Ferry and Charles Town, and a church kitchen in Hedgesville. Not sure if you are in range? Call the showroom.

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: The whole process of planning, designing, ordering, scheduling and installing can take 3 to 6 months. Most of that time comes before work begins. Once the project starts, a typical Mountaineer kitchen remodel takes about 2 to 3 weeks. Material choices, the size of the job and its complexity all affect the timing.

items.q: When can I visit the showroom?
items.a: The showroom at 1950 Rock Cliff Dr in Martinsburg is open Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm. Saturday and Sunday visits are by appointment only, which helps if you cannot get there during the workday. Call (304) 267-6262 to set a time, or just stop in during the week for ideas.

items.q: Do you do all the work yourselves?
items.a: Yes. Mountaineer's in-house team handles every project from start to finish. On recent kitchens that meant demolition, plumbing changes for a new stove, vent ducting, drywall, cabinet installation, trim, toe-kicks and hardware. On one Harpers Ferry kitchen it also meant the engineering coordination for a load-bearing wall.

items.q: How do you keep a shower from leaking?
items.a: Recent showers are built on Schluter shower pans, with Kerdi waterproofing membrane on the walls before tile goes up. The Reap master bath in Harpers Ferry used a 72-inch Schluter pan with a curbless entry. The Dagg shower in Charles Town used the same system, plus a built-in bench and dual niches.

Yes. Mountaineer offers financing through Acorn for customers who would rather not pay the full cost up front. Ask about it when you visit the showroom or call (304) 267-6262. Terms and approval come from the lender, so the team can point you to the application while you plan your kitchen or bath.

final_cta.h2: Come see it in person on Rock Cliff Drive
final_cta.text: Visit the showroom weekdays 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, or call to book a weekend appointment with Ben's team.
